services_hero_desc: From precision CNC machining to advanced 3D printing, we offer comprehensive manufacturing solutions to turn your designs into reality.
service_cnc-machining_capability_1: Precision machining with tolerances as tight as ±0.01mm
service_cnc-machining_capability_3: Materials include aluminum, steel, copper, plastics, and more
service_cnc-machining_faq_quote_speed_qu: How quickly can I get a quote for precision CNC machining services?
service_cnc-machining_faq_quote_speed_an: At Microns Hub, we prioritize speed without compromising accuracy. You can upload your CAD files directly through our platform and receive a detailed, competitive quote within 24 hours. Our system analyzes your design for manufacturability to ensure accurate pricing and rapid turnaround times.
service_cnc-machining_faq_tolerances_que: What are the standard and tightest tolerances you can achieve with CNC machining?
service_cnc-machining_faq_tolerances_ans: Our standard CNC machining tolerance is ISO 2768-m, suitable for most functional metal and plastic parts. For high-precision applications—such as aerospace or medical components—we can achieve tight tolerances of ±0.01 mm (10 microns). Please specify critical dimensions in your technical drawings (PDF).
service_cnc-machining_faq_materials_ques: What materials are available for custom CNC machined parts?
service_cnc-machining_faq_materials_answ: We offer a vast selection of certified metals and engineering plastics. Our inventory includes Aluminum (AL6061, AL7075, AL5083), Stainless Steel (304, 316L, 17-4PH), Titanium (Grade 5), and Tool Steels. We also machine high-performance plastics like POM (Delrin), PEEK, and Polycarbonate.
service_cnc-machining_faq_5axis_question: When should I choose 5-axis CNC milling over 3-axis machining?
service_cnc-machining_faq_5axis_answer: 3-axis milling is cost-effective for parts with simple geometries machined from one side. 5-axis CNC milling is ideal for complex parts with intricate features, deep cavities, or undercuts, as it allows the tool to approach the workpiece from all angles, improving precision and reducing setup time.
service_cnc-machining_faq_prototyping_qu: Do you handle both rapid prototyping and low-volume production runs?
service_cnc-machining_faq_prototyping_an: Yes, Microns Hub is built to scale. We offer rapid prototyping (from 1 piece) to validate designs quickly, as well as low-to-mid volume production (100–10,000+ parts). Our network allows us to transition you seamlessly from prototype to series production without minimum order quantity (MOQ) bottlenecks.
service_cnc-machining_faq_surface_finish: What surface finishes and post-processing options do you offer?

We provide comprehensive post-processing to ensure parts are end-use ready. Finishes include As-Machined, Bead Blasting (matte), Anodizing (Type II/III), Passivation, Electroplating, Powder Coating, and Heat Treatment. These treatments enhance wear resistance, corrosion protection, and aesthetics.
service_cnc-machining_faq_quality_questi: How do you ensure the quality of CNC machined parts?
service_cnc-machining_faq_quality_answer: Quality is paramount. We work with manufacturing partners who follow strict ISO 9001 certified processes. Every order undergoes rigorous quality control, including Material Certification (available upon request) and 100% part inspection for critical dimensions before shipment.
service_cnc-machining_faq_cost_factors_q: What factors most significantly impact the cost of CNC machining?
service_cnc-machining_faq_cost_factors_a: The main cost drivers are machining time, material cost, and complexity. To reduce costs, we recommend using standard hole sizes, avoiding deep cavities, minimizing tight tolerances to only necessary features, and reducing the number of required part orientations (setups).
service_cnc-machining_faq_max_dimensions: What are the maximum part dimensions you can machine?

We can handle large-format machining projects. Our network capabilities allow for maximum part dimensions of up to 7500 mm x 3000 mm x 2200 mm. Whether you need small connectors or large structural components, we have the capacity to accommodate your size requirements.
service_cnc-machining_faq_cad_formats_qu: Which CAD file formats do you accept for quoting and manufacturing?
service_cnc-machining_faq_cad_formats_an: For the fastest quoting, please upload 3D CAD files in STEP (.stp/.step) format. We also accept IGES, X_T, and SolidWorks files. For tolerances, threads, and specific surface finish requirements, please accompany your 3D model with a 2D technical drawing (PDF).
service_sheet-metal_capability_2: CNC press brake bending up to 4m length
service_sheet-metal_capability_3: MIG, TIG, and spot welding capabilities
service_sheet-metal_capability_4: Various metal types including steel, aluminum, and stainless steel
service_sheet-metal_capability_5: Surface finishing options including powder coating and plating
service_sheet-metal_faq_max_size_questio: What is the maximum sheet size and thickness for laser cutting services?
service_sheet-metal_faq_max_size_answer: We can process sheet metal parts with maximum dimensions up to 2500 x 1250 mm. Our laser cutting capabilities handle material thicknesses ranging from 0.5 mm up to 25 mm, ensuring versatility for both delicate enclosures and heavy-duty structural brackets.
service_sheet-metal_faq_tolerances_quest: What standard tolerances apply to your sheet metal fabrication?
service_sheet-metal_faq_tolerances_answe: For laser cutting and CNC bending, our standard general tolerance is ±0.1 mm. Tighter tolerances may be achievable depending on the feature and material thickness; please indicate critical dimensions on your 2D drawings for engineering review.
service_sheet-metal_faq_materials_questi: Which materials are commonly stocked for sheet metal projects?
service_sheet-metal_faq_materials_answer: We stock a wide range of sheet metals, including Aluminum (5052, 6061, 7075), Stainless Steel (304, 316/316L), Mild Steel (CRS, HRPO), Galvanized Steel, Copper, and Brass. Specialized alloys can also be sourced upon request.
service_sheet-metal_faq_hardware_questio: Can you provide sheet metal parts with pre-installed hardware?
service_sheet-metal_faq_hardware_answer: Yes, we offer full assembly services including the insertion of fasteners such as PEM nuts, studs, and standoffs. We also perform welding (MIG, TIG, Spot) and riveting to deliver complete, ready-to-assemble components.
service_sheet-metal_faq_surface_finishes: What surface finishes are recommended for sheet metal parts?

To prevent corrosion and improve aesthetics, we offer Powder Coating (in various RAL colors), Anodizing (for aluminum), Zinc Plating, Chromating, and Brushing. We can advise on the best finish based on your part's operating environment.
service_sheet-metal_faq_bending_question: Do you offer bending and forming for complex geometries?
service_sheet-metal_faq_bending_answer: Absolutely. We utilize CNC-controlled press brakes to create accurate bends and complex forms. Our equipment supports multiple bend angles and complicated geometries, ensuring repeatability across production batches.
service_sheet-metal_faq_moq_question: Is there a minimum order quantity (MOQ) for sheet metal fabrication?
service_sheet-metal_faq_moq_answer: No, we support projects starting from a single prototype (Batch size: 1) up to high-volume production runs. Our agile manufacturing setup allows us to be cost-effective for both one-off custom parts and large series.
service_sheet-metal_faq_design_files_que: How do I prepare my design files for sheet metal fabrication?
service_sheet-metal_faq_design_files_ans: For the best results, please submit a 3D STEP file representing the folded part and a 2D PDF drawing specifying threads, tolerances, and finishing requirements. Ensure your design accounts for bend radii and material deformation (K-factor).
service_sheet-metal_faq_lead_time_questi: What is the typical lead time for sheet metal parts?
service_sheet-metal_faq_lead_time_answer: Our optimized workflow allows for fast turnarounds. Depending on complexity and quantity, we can ship sheet metal prototypes in as little as 3–5 business days, helping you accelerate your product development cycle.
service_sheet-metal_faq_redesign_questio: Can you help redesign a machined part for sheet metal fabrication to save costs?
service_sheet-metal_faq_redesign_answer: Yes, converting machined parts to sheet metal is a common cost-reduction strategy. Our engineering team can review your design and suggest modifications—such as replacing solid blocks with bent sheet metal—to significantly lower material usage and production costs.
service_3d-printing_capability_1: SLA, SLS, FDM, and MJF technologies
service_3d-printing_capability_3: Various materials including plastics, resins, and nylon
service_3d-printing_capability_4: Complex geometries impossible with traditional manufacturing
service_3d-printing_capability_5: On-demand production with no tooling costs
service_3d-printing_capability_6: Quick turnaround times starting at 24 hours
service_3d-printing_faq_technologies_que: Which 3D printing technologies are available at Microns Hub?
service_3d-printing_faq_technologies_ans: We offer a suite of industrial additive manufacturing technologies, including FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) for rapid prototypes, SLA (Stereolithography) for high-detail visual models, SLS (Selective Laser Sintering) for functional nylon parts, and MJF (Multi Jet Fusion) for production-grade components.
service_3d-printing_faq_materials_questi: What materials can I choose for 3D printed parts?
service_3d-printing_faq_materials_answer: Our material range covers rigid and flexible options. Common materials include PLA and ABS for basic fit checks, Nylon (PA12) for functional durability, Resins for smooth details, and high-performance thermoplastics like PEEK or Carbon-Filled Nylon for engineering applications.
service_3d-printing_faq_vs_cnc_question: How does 3D printing compare to CNC machining for prototyping?
service_3d-printing_faq_vs_cnc_answer: 3D printing is generally faster and more cost-effective for complex geometries and low quantities, as it requires no tooling. CNC machining is better for testing the actual production material and achieving tighter tolerances. We can help you decide the best method for your specific project phase.
service_3d-printing_faq_large_parts_ques: Can you print large parts in a single piece?
service_3d-printing_faq_large_parts_answ: Yes, we have large-format printers capable of producing bulky components. For parts exceeding our build volumes, we can print in sections and professionally bond them to create full-scale models with high structural integrity.
service_3d-printing_faq_end_use_question: Is 3D printing suitable for end-use production parts?
service_3d-printing_faq_end_use_answer: Absolutely. Technologies like SLS and MJF produce isotropic, durable parts suitable for end-use applications in automotive, medical, and industrial machinery. These parts can be post-processed to look and perform like injection-molded components.
service_3d-printing_faq_resolution_quest: What is the typical layer height and resolution?
service_3d-printing_faq_resolution_answe: Resolution depends on the technology. SLA and PolyJet can achieve layer heights as fine as 0.02–0.05 mm for smooth surfaces. FDM typically ranges from 0.1–0.3 mm, while SLS/MJF usually prints at 0.08–0.1 mm, offering a balance of speed and detail.
service_3d-printing_faq_post_processing_: Do you offer post-processing for 3D printed parts?
Yes, we offer vapor smoothing (to seal surfaces), sandblasting, dyeing (coloring nylon parts), and painting. These finishes improve the mechanical properties and visual quality of the printed parts.
service_3d-printing_faq_file_formats_que: What file formats are required for 3D printing quotes?
service_3d-printing_faq_file_formats_ans: The standard format for 3D printing is STL, but we also accept STEP and IGES files. Please ensure your mesh is "watertight" (manifold) to prevent slicing errors and ensure an accurate quote.
service_3d-printing_faq_speed_question: How quickly can I receive my 3D printed parts?
service_3d-printing_faq_speed_answer: 3D printing is our fastest service. We can often produce and ship parts within 24–48 hours after order confirmation, making it the ideal solution for urgent prototyping needs.
service_3d-printing_faq_flexible_questio: Can 3D printing produce flexible or rubber-like parts?
service_3d-printing_faq_flexible_answer: Yes, we print with flexible materials such as TPU (Thermoplastic Polyurethane) and various shore-hardness resins. These are perfect for prototyping gaskets, seals, grips, and vibration dampers.
service_injection-molding_capability_3: Wide range of thermoplastics and elastomers
service_injection-molding_capability_4: Parts with complex geometries and features
service_injection-molding_capability_5: High volume capability up to millions of parts
service_injection-molding_capability_6: Secondary operations including assembly and finishing
service_injection-molding_faq_min_quanti: What is the minimum quantity for injection molding orders?

While injection molding is typically for mass production, we offer bridge tooling and low-volume runs starting from as few as 500 units. This allows you to bridge the gap between prototyping and full-scale mass production without a massive initial investment.
service_injection-molding_faq_tooling_qu: Do you offer rapid tooling (aluminum molds) or just steel molds?
service_injection-molding_faq_tooling_an: We offer both. Aluminum molds are faster and cheaper to manufacture, ideal for low-volume runs (up to 10,000 shots). Hardened steel molds are available for high-volume production (100,000+ shots) requiring maximum durability and cycle speed.
service_injection-molding_faq_plastics_q: What types of plastics can be injection molded?
service_injection-molding_faq_plastics_a: We mold a comprehensive range of thermoplastics, including commodity plastics like PP, PE, and PS, and engineering-grade materials like ABS, PC, Nylon (PA6/PA66), PBT, POM, and TPE/TPU. We can also include additives like glass fiber or UV stabilizers.
service_injection-molding_faq_overmoldin: Can you handle overmolding and insert molding?

Yes, we specialize in overmolding (e.g., soft rubber grips over hard plastic) and insert molding (encapsulating metal inserts like threaded brass nuts). These processes improve part functionality and eliminate secondary assembly steps.
service_injection-molding_faq_mold_time_: How long does it take to manufacture a mold?

Lead times vary by complexity. Simple rapid tooling can be ready in 2–4 weeks, while complex multi-cavity production molds typically take 4–8 weeks. We provide a detailed timeline with your DFM (Design for Manufacturability) report.
service_injection-molding_faq_mold_owner: Who owns the mold after production?

You do. Once you pay for the tooling, the mold is your property. We store and maintain it at our facility for your future production runs, ensuring it remains in optimal condition for its guaranteed lifespan.
service_injection-molding_faq_dfm_questi: Do you provide a DFM analysis before cutting the mold?
service_injection-molding_faq_dfm_answer: Yes, every injection molding order includes a comprehensive DFM analysis. Our engineers review your design for draft angles, wall thickness consistency, gate locations, and ejection issues to prevent defects and ensure a high-quality outcome.
service_injection-molding_faq_accuracy_q: How accurate are injection molded parts?
service_injection-molding_faq_accuracy_a: Injection molding offers high precision and repeatability. Standard tolerances are typically ±0.1 mm to ±0.2 mm, but tighter tolerances can be achieved with precision tooling and specific material selection.
service_injection-molding_faq_colors_que: Can you match specific brand colors (Pantone/RAL)?
service_injection-molding_faq_colors_ans: Absolutely. We use masterbatches or pre-compounded resins to match your specific Pantone or RAL color codes. This ensures your parts align perfectly with your brand identity and product design requirements.
service_injection-molding_faq_textures_q: What surface textures are available for molded parts?
service_injection-molding_faq_textures_a: We can apply industry-standard textures, such as VDI 3400 or Mold-Tech finishes, directly to the mold cavity. Options range from high-gloss polish to heavy matte or grain textures to hide sink marks and improve grip.
service_surface-finish_faq_importance_qu: Why is surface finishing important for manufactured parts?
service_surface-finish_faq_importance_an: Surface finishing is critical for both functionality and aesthetics. It improves corrosion resistance, hardness, electrical conductivity, and wear resistance, while also removing machining marks to provide a professional, consumer-ready look.
service_surface-finish_faq_anodizing_typ: What is the difference between Anodizing Type II and Type III?

Type II Anodizing is decorative, providing corrosion resistance and a wide range of color options. Type III (Hardcoat) Anodizing creates a much thicker, harder ceramic-like layer, offering superior wear resistance and electrical insulation for harsh industrial environments.
service_surface-finish_faq_powder_coatin: Can you color-match parts using Powder Coating?

Yes, Powder Coating is available in a vast array of RAL and Pantone colors. It provides a durable, uniform finish that is more resistant to chipping and scratching than traditional wet paint, making it ideal for enclosures and architectural parts.
service_surface-finish_faq_passivation_q: What is passivation and which materials require it?
service_surface-finish_faq_passivation_a: Passivation is a chemical process used primarily for Stainless Steel. It removes free iron from the surface and enhances the formation of a passive oxide layer, significantly improving the material's natural corrosion resistance without altering dimensions.
service_surface-finish_faq_bead_blasting: How does bead blasting affect part tolerances?

Bead blasting removes material very slightly to create a matte, uniform texture. While generally negligible, it can affect extremely tight tolerances (e.g., < 0.01mm). We recommend masking critical features like bearing bores or threads during the blasting process.
service_surface-finish_faq_electroless_n: What is Electroless Nickel Plating used for?

Electroless Nickel Plating deposits a uniform layer of nickel-phosphorus alloy on complex geometries. It is excellent for corrosion protection, hardness, and lubricity, and unlike electrolytic plating, it ensures even thickness across all surfaces, including internal cavities.
service_surface-finish_faq_black_oxide_q: Do you offer Black Oxide finishing?
service_surface-finish_faq_black_oxide_a: Yes, Black Oxide is a conversion coating for ferrous metals, stainless steel, and copper. It adds mild corrosion resistance and minimizes light reflection. It is commonly used on gears, fasteners, and tools where dimensional change must be minimized.
service_surface-finish_faq_mirror_finish: Can you polish parts to a mirror finish?

We offer mechanical polishing and electropolishing to achieve low Ra (roughness average) values, up to a mirror-like finish. This is essential for medical devices, food processing equipment, and high-end aesthetic components.
service_surface-finish_faq_surface_rough: What is the standard surface roughness (Ra) for CNC parts?

The standard "as-machined" finish is typically Ra 3.2 μm, where visible tool marks remain. We can refine this to Ra 1.6, 0.8, or 0.4 μm through smoothing and polishing processes depending on your requirements.
service_surface-finish_faq_multiple_fini: Can you apply multiple finishes to a single part?

Yes, we can perform selective finishing. For example, we can anodize an aluminum part and then CNC machine specific areas to expose the raw metal for electrical grounding (masking), or apply chromate conversion to internal surfaces while powder coating the exterior.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_speed_ques: How fast can Microns Hub deliver rapid prototypes?
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_speed_answ: Speed is our core strength. Depending on the complexity and technology chosen, we can manufacture and ship prototypes in as little as 3 business days. Our digital quoting system helps accelerate the process by providing instant pricing and DFM feedback.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_functional: Which technology is best for a functional prototype?

For functional testing where material strength matters, CNC Machining or SLS 3D Printing (Nylon) are best. If you need to test fit and form only, FDM or SLA 3D printing offers a faster and more cost-effective solution.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_production: Can I prototype in the actual production material?

Yes. With CNC Machining and Sheet Metal Fabrication, we use the exact stock materials (e.g., Aluminum 6061, SS304) intended for your final product, ensuring your prototype's mechanical and thermal properties match the production units 100%.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_prototype_: Is it possible to move from prototyping to production with the same supplier?

Absolutely. Microns Hub is a one-stop shop. We help you iterate through rapid prototyping and, once the design is frozen, seamlessly scale up to low-volume or mass production using our injection molding or extensive CNC network, keeping all your data in one place.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_vacuum_cas: Do you offer Vacuum Casting for prototypes?

Yes, Vacuum Casting (Urethane Casting) is excellent for producing 10–50 high-quality copies of a master pattern. It simulates injection molded parts in terms of surface finish and material properties (rigid or flexible) without the high cost of metal tooling.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_ip_questio: How do you handle intellectual property (IP) for prototypes?
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_ip_answer: We take IP protection seriously. We operate under strict EU laws and are happy to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before you upload any files. Your designs are shared only with the vetted partners strictly necessary to manufacture your parts.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_assemblies: Yes, we can manufacture multi-component assemblies. We can produce the metal housing via sheet metal, the internal brackets via CNC, and the plastic covers via 3D printing, delivering a complete works-like prototype for your review.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_cost_diffe: What is the cost difference between 3D printing and CNC for a single prototype?

Generally, 3D printing is cheaper for a single unit with complex geometry. CNC machining has higher setup costs but becomes competitive as quantities increase or if the part requires the strength of solid metal. Our instant quote tool allows you to compare prices for both instantly.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_file_types: What file types do I need to send for a prototyping quote?

A 3D CAD file (STEP, STL, IGES) is sufficient for most prototyping quotes. If your prototype requires specific tolerances, threads, or surface finishes, please include a 2D drawing to ensure we meet your functional requirements.
service_rapid-prototyping_faq_design_fee: Can you provide design feedback during the prototyping phase?

Yes, our "Engineer-Reviewed" process means we check your files for manufacturability issues (like thin walls or impossible undercuts) before production. This feedback loop helps you refine your design early, saving time and money before you commit to expensive production tools.

quote_page_faq_manufacturing_time_answer: Typical lead times range from 1-3 weeks depending on complexity and quantity. We offer expedited options for urgent projects.
quote_page_faq_quote_info_question: What information do I need for a quote?
quote_page_faq_quote_info_answer: We need your CAD files, material preferences, quantity requirements, and any specific tolerances or surface finish requirements.
quote_page_faq_min_order_question: Is there a minimum order quantity?
